title: Valhalla: A Layered Knowledge-State and Service-Governance Framework for Long-Term Scientific Knowledge Work
abstract: arXiv:2608.15193v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly adopted in scientific research, external knowledge bases, knowledge graphs, and long-term memory have improved information retrieval and task continuity. However, most structured knowledge systems remain node-centric, representing files, concepts, results, and judgments as nodes and relations in a graph. While suitable for personal knowledge management, such structures often depend on individual organizational practices, limiting knowledge sharing, integration, and reorganization across users. This paper presents Valhalla, a layered knowledge-state and service-governance framework for long-term scientific knowledge work. Valhalla replaces flat graphs with layered encapsulation and stable semantic boundaries through a five-layer File-Resource-Entity-Relationship-Graph (FREG) model. translated_title: Valhalla：一种用于长期科学知识工作的分层知识状态与服务治理框架
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）代理在科学研究中的日益普及，外部知识库、知识图谱和长期记忆已改善了信息检索和任务连续性。然而，大多数结构化知识系统仍以节点为中心，将文件、概念、结果和判断表示为图中的节点和关系。虽然这种结构适用于个人知识管理，但往往依赖于个体的组织实践，限制了跨用户的知识共享、集成和重组。本文提出了Valhalla，一种用于长期科学知识工作的分层知识状态与服务治理框架。Valhalla通过五层文件-资源-实体-关系-图（FREG）模型，用分层封装和稳定的语义边界取代了扁平图。文件和资源层保留了源身份和来源，实体层表示知识对象，关系层管理语义连接。
tldr: Valhalla提出了一种五层FREG分层框架，通过稳定的语义边界和来源保留，解决了现有节点中心知识系统在跨用户共享和集成上的局限性，提升了长期科学知识工作的治理效率。
en_tdlr: Valhalla introduces a five-layer FREG framework with stable semantic boundaries and provenance preservation, addressing the limitations of node-centric knowledge systems in cross-user sharing and integration, thereby enhancing governance in long-term scientific knowledge work.
